chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is recommended to perform three hundred and sixty circuits (usbu'at), corresponding to the number of days of the year. If you are unable, then three hundred and sixty shawt (lengths of the circumambulation path). If you are unable, then whatever you are able to do of the circumambulation. And whoever vows to circumambulate upon four, let him perform two circuits: one circuit for his hands and one circuit for his feet. He narrated that.

key_terms.أُسْبُوعاً: A circuit or round (specifically a longer measure in this context)
key_terms.شَوْطاً: A length or span of the path

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended number of tawaf circuits and how is a vow of 'four' interpreted?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the recommended practice of performing 360 *usbu'at* (half-circuits) to mirror the solar year, offering a graded concession down to *shawt* (lengths) for those with limited capacity. It further clarifies the specific ritual interpretation of a vow to circumambulate 'upon four' as two full circuits, distinguishing between the upper and lower body movements. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on flexibility in voluntary worship while maintaining precise adherence to the physical mechanics of the ritual.
